question.knowledge_point: Simplifying an Expression by Expanding Parentheses and Using the Pythagorean Identity
question.worked_solution:
First, we expand the parentheses:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡t(\operatorname{sin}⁡t-1)+{cos}^{2}⁡t & ={sin}^{2}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t \\  & =({sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t)-\operatorname{sin}⁡t \\  & =1-\operatorname{sin}⁡t\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that, in the last step, we simplified the right-hand side using ${cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t=1.$ 

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡t(\operatorname{sin}⁡t-1)+{cos}^{2}⁡t=1-\operatorname{sin}⁡t.
$$
